subject: CAIQ deliverables — Celestia evidence bundle & owner commitments

From: Claire Jensen <claire.j@celestiahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ken Ortiz <ken.ortiz@celestiahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 17:12:00 -0400
Subject: Celestia CAIQ intake and timeline

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team compiled the CAIQ (v4) and would like Redwood's completed response plus supporting evidence for review. High level asks:

- Completed CAIQ spreadsheet (we prefer one row per question with answer and evidence pointer)
- Plain-language control trace that maps CAIQ IDs to Redwood controls and owners
- Packaged evidence (PDFs, diagrams) we can drop into our intake portal

Can you confirm who on your side will own each control so we can start intake processing? We ideally need the delivered package by EOD Friday, May 22.

Also: a few CAIQ items will need short notes for how you handle KV caching and telemetry retention — security wants explicit file references.

Thanks,
Claire Jensen
Director, Information Security
Celestia Health

Attachments: Celestia_CAIQ_v4.xlsx (original questionnaire)

Team — forwarding Celestia's CAIQ intake. They're asking for a completed spreadsheet, a control trace, and packaged evidence by EOD Friday (May 22). Their point about KV caching and telemetry retention needs short, clear notes.

Proposed split:
- Mina: assemble the CAIQ answers and attach evidence PDFs.
- Laura: produce the control trace mapping CAIQ IDs to Redwood controls + owner column.
- Vanessa: export architecture/network diagram and confirm where telemetry logs live and retention windows.

Claire is cc'd so we can ask clarifying questions if needed. If any item slips, call it out now so I can reset expectations.

Thanks — Marcus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Celestia CAIQ intake and timeline

Marcus / team / Claire —

Attached is the deliverable set for Celestia:
- CLST-CAIQ-answered-20270522.xlsx — completed CAIQ with per-question answer + evidence pointer (column H).
- evidence-index-CLST-20270522.pdf — consolidated index listing file names, authors, and internal retention notes.
- network-diagram-clst.png — trimmed architecture diagram suitable for intake portal.

Highlights / notes:
- KV cache behaviour (CAIQ section CCM-5): we use an in-memory KV cache with eviction based on LRU; persistent KV (for sharded KV checkpoints) is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and documented in evidence-index (file: kv-encryption-note.pdf).
- Telemetry / logs (CAIQ section LOG-2): operational telemetry is retained in our logging tier for 90 days by default; aggregated metrics are stored for 365 days. See evidence-index references log-retention-policy.pdf and splunk-index-config.txt.
- Control owners: Laura has populated the crosswalk sheet (tab "Control Trace") with owner email and sprint commitments for any changes.

Open items I flagged for response:
1) Claire asked for any third-party subprocessors used for logging — I've called out Splunk Cloud (log aggregation) and S3 (artifact storage) with versions and contract references in the index.
2) A couple of CAIQ items (identity federation exceptions) require product notes from Product Security; Laura, can you add a short note where applicable?

I'll upload the full zipped bundle to the Drive link below. If Celestia's intake portal needs files named differently, tell me and I will rename prior to upload.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: CLST-CAIQ-answered-20270522.xlsx; evidence-index-CLST-20270522.pdf; network-diagram-clst.png

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-CLST-CAIQ

Mina / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and thorough package. A couple quick clarifying questions before I push this into our portal:

1) In the evidence-index the kv-encryption-note.pdf references an internal key management design doc. Can you confirm if keys for KV checkpoints are customer-specific and whether they're in our region (we're US-east)?

2) For telemetry retention: can you supply the exact Splunk index names used for ingestion so my ops team can map them into our SOC runbooks? The index names are fine to share, but please avoid any PII in the payloads.

If you can reply to those two points today, we can proceed. Appreciate the detailed crosswalk — that made review much faster on our side.

Claire
Director, Information Security
Celestia Health
